lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: Pythagorean relationship

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: In a right triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?

steps: Identify the legs and the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle.
Use a² + b² = c² and take a square root only after finding c².
workedSolution.answer: the side opposite the right angle

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 9 and 5. What is its hypotenuse in simplest radical form?
Do the points (0, 0), (3, 0), and (0, 4) form a right triangle?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Do side lengths 5, 12, and 14 satisfy the Pythagorean theorem?
choices: only if both legs are equal
only if the triangle is acute

items.prompt: Classify a triangle with side lengths 5, 12, and 13 using the converse of the Pythagorean theorem.
What is the distance between (0, 0) and (11, 8) in simplest radical form?
Do the points (0, 0), (7, 0), and (0, 24) form a right triangle?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A rectangle is 10 units by 10 units. What is the length of its diagonal in simplest radical form?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A 25-ft ladder reaches 24 ft up a vertical wall. How far is its base from the wall?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
